subject: E-Commerce
title: The End of the Shopping Cart
description: A quick win: understand The End of the Shopping Cart.

hook.text: The shopping cart icon was designed in 1995. It mimics pushing a physical cart through aisles that don't exist online.

buildup.text: Online shopping borrowed every metaphor from physical retail: carts, checkouts, aisles, and storefronts.

discovery.text: Future commerce won't need carts. AI agents will negotiate, purchase, and arrange delivery.

twist.text: Removing the cart removes browsing, comparison, and deliberation. The joy of shopping may vanish with the friction.

climax.text: E-commerce started by copying physical retail. The future throws away those metaphors entirely for something new.

punchline.text: The cart icon is from 1995. Shopping's future won't resemble today's model.

quiz.question: Why might removing the shopping cart metaphor change the experience?
options: It eliminates browsing and deliberation, removing both friction and the joy of exploration
